I was raised by a single mom. Every December for as long as I can remember while I lived at home she would write down 25 random acts of kindness on small slips of paper and we would draw one every day of december. Some were small things like buying someones lunch, others took more time or effort. Ironically they always seemed to cause more trouble than the deed was worth because people were so confused. I think my favorite that I remember was when she thought it would be a great idea to get a bunch of groceries and leave them on the porch of someone that she thought could use them (I think it might have been a family she had encountered through work (social worker at the time)). The look on their face when they came out as we were driving away...just...so confused. I'm an atheist now and don't really celebrate christmas but I might do this with my kids one day, at least for the memories and to push them outside of their comfort zone.

I live in house that has been converted into two apartments. Our neighbors (a couple) moved out at the beginning of August, and we got a new neighbor (a college student). During the first week she moved in, I was going to take out our garbage on pick-up day, and we hadn't met our new neighbor yet. We just knew that she had moved in that week. I typically take the trash out the night before pick-up because they come at like 3 in the morning. And when I went to take it out, I saw all of her trash sitting next to her door. There was so much that it was overflowing, and things were just all around it. And since it was like midnight, I didn't want to wake her or anything, so I took all of it down to the curb for her. And then the next morning after they picked it up, I brought her garbage bin back to her front door.

But the cool thing is that, by just being a decent human being, I think she figured out when trash day was, and realized I had done her a solid. So, now, it's turned into this thing where, whoever is taking their trash out first, just grabs all of the stuff for both apartments and does it, and whoever leaves first in the morning takes it all back. I've never shared chores with a neighbor before, but I really enjoy it a great deal.
